---
title: "table() does not count NAs"
ref: LEN-09
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'sum(table(c("a", NA, "a")))'
reponse: '2'
attendu: "`3`, the number of values"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
answers <- c("yes", "no", NA, "yes", NA)
table(answers)
sum(table(answers))
length(answers)
```
:::

## Why

By default, `table()` drops missing values before counting, without saying so. The table looks complete, but its counts do not add up to the number of observations.

Proportions computed afterwards with `prop.table()` then only cover the known answers. That may be intended, but it is rarely a conscious decision.

## The fix

Ask for the `NA`s explicitly with `useNA = "ifany"`, which adds an `<NA>` column only when there are some.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
table(answers, useNA = "ifany")
```
:::
